name: PCP
description: PCP (angel dust) facts: effects, agitation and violence risks, overdose signs, why it is Schedule II, dependence, and federal penalties.
quick: PCP (phencyclidine), also called angel dust, is a dissociative drug developed as an anesthetic in the 1950s and abandoned because of severe agitation and hallucinations in patients. It is Schedule II because it was once a medicine, but it has no current medical use. It can cause psychosis, violent agitation, dangerously high body temperature, and muscle breakdown.
facts: Angel dust, wet, sherm, love boat, embalming fluid

blocks.p: PCP was developed in the 1950s as a surgical anesthetic (Sernyl) but was withdrawn for human use in 1965 because patients developed agitation, delusions, and irrational behavior on waking. Ketamine was later developed as a safer relative.[[1]]
It is sold as a liquid, powder, or tablets. Cigarettes or joints dipped in liquid PCP are called "wet" or "sherm".

sections.q: What are the effects of pcp, and how long do they last?

blocks.p: At low doses PCP causes numbness, a drunk-like feeling, and detachment. At higher doses it causes hallucinations, paranoia, agitation, loss of contact with reality, inability to feel pain, rapid eye movements, high blood pressure, and drooling.[[1]]
Effects start within minutes when smoked and last about 4 to 6 hours, but some people stay disturbed for a day or more.

sections.q: What are the risks of pcp?

blocks.p: **Agitation and injury:** people on PCP may become violent or panicked and, unable to feel pain, can seriously injure themselves.[[1]]
**Physical dangers:** very high body temperature, muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) leading to kidney failure, seizures, and very high blood pressure.[[1]]
**Mental health:** psychosis resembling schizophrenia, memory problems, depression, and speech difficulties after long-term use.

sections.q: What does a PCP overdose look like?

blocks.p: Signs include severe agitation or catatonia, rapid involuntary eye movements, very high temperature, very high blood pressure, muscle rigidity, seizures, and coma. Dark urine can signal muscle breakdown.[[1]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, breathing slowly, having a seizure, very hot, or violently agitated.
Place an unresponsive person on their side so they do not choke if they vomit.
Keep them away from roads, water, and heights. People on dissociatives often cannot feel pain or judge danger.
If opioids could be involved, give naloxone. It will not harm the person.

blocks.p: Keep a safe distance from a severely agitated person, remove dangerous objects, keep the environment quiet and dim, and call 911.

sections.q: Is pcp addictive, and what is withdrawal like?

blocks.p: Repeated PCP use can cause tolerance, cravings, and compulsive use. Stopping after regular use can cause depression, cravings, headaches, and sweating.[[1]]

timeline.title: Recovery
timeline.text: Memory and mood problems may persist.

sections.q: Is pcp legal in the US?

blocks.p: PCP is Schedule II because it once had an accepted medical use as an anesthetic. Today it has no approved use and is not manufactured legally for medicine.[[2]]

ul: **Possession:** under federal law, a first conviction for possessing any controlled substance without a valid prescription can bring up to one year in prison and a minimum fine of $1,000. Penalties rise with prior convictions.[[3]]
**Trafficking:** trafficking 10 grams or more of pure PCP, or 100 grams or more of a mixture, carries a mandatory minimum of 5 years in federal prison; ten times those amounts carries 10 years.[[4]]

**State law:** states set their own penalties, and most drug cases are prosecuted under state law. Penalties range from a civil fine to long prison terms depending on the state, the amount, and prior record.

sections.q: Where can someone get help with pcp use?

ul: **SAMHSA National Helpline:** 1-800-662-4357. Free, confidential, 24 hours a day, in English and Spanish. It gives referrals to local treatment and support.[[5]]
**FindTreatment.gov:** a federal locator for state-licensed treatment programs, searchable by location, payment, and type of care.[[6]]
**988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline:** call or text 988 for a mental health or substance use crisis.
**Your own clinician:** a primary care doctor can screen, treat, and refer, and can discuss medicines that support recovery where they exist.

faq: Why is PCP Schedule II and not Schedule I?
Because it was once approved as an anesthetic. It has no current medical use.
Is PCP the same as ketamine?
They are related dissociatives, but PCP is far longer-lasting and more likely to cause agitation and psychosis.
How long does PCP stay in your system?
Its half-life is about 21 hours. Urine tests can detect it for about a week, and longer after heavy use.
What is a sherm or wet joint?
A cigarette or joint dipped in liquid PCP.
